headline: No votes on policy or funding; board heard updates on $35M library renovation, Capital Campaign goal of $23M by January, and summer programs.
summary: The board reviewed Friends of FFL updates, including a fall book sale, Mini Golf planning for March 2027, and progress on the $35M renovation project with a goal of $23M raised by January. The Director presented data on an embedded social worker from the Howard Street Team, and staff reported on the 2026 Summer Challenge Program. No policy decisions were made.
plain_text:
LIBRARY BOARD of COMMISSIONERS 
Wednesday, September 16, 2026, 7:45 am 
Minutes 
 
Present: Gale Batsimm, Megan Butterfield, Jonathan Chapple-Sokol, Emily Copeland, Mary Danko, Chol Dhoor, 
Patrick Halladay, Cate MacLachlan, Amy Mellencamp, Wells Shelley, Lydia Spinner, Nick Tatakis, Rebecca 
Thompson, Mona Tolba. 
 
Approval of minutes: from July 15. Patrick Halladay moved, Cate MacLachlan seconded, approved. 
 
Approval of agenda: Cate MacLachlan moved, Patrick Halladay seconded, approved. 
 
Public Forum: No public in attendance.  
 
Friends of FFL Report: Friends fall book sale starts today and runs through the weekend. Friends Mini Golf 
committee is planning Mini Golf on March 19 & 20, 2027. The Friends are also planning for where they will be 
during the renovation. Capital Committee update is that they are hiring a Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) as 
the BSD did. The Building Committee is meeting regularly. The Capital Campaign committee is working on a video. 
The goal is to have $23M by January for the $35M project. 
Director’s Report: Mary showed slides of the data from the first year of having an embedded social worker from 
the Howard Street Team at the library. This is the information she presented to City Council.  
Staff Report: Megan presented on the 2026 Summer Challenge Program. There were many wonderful programs 
related to the Unearth A Story theme including Dino Dig, Dino Cakes, Dinoman , VINS (raptors), a Treasure Hunt, 
etc. A new site was added at the Intervale this year, which grew in popularity as folks learned the library would be 
present—families began bringing their children. 
Subcommittee update: 
Policy Committee will be meeting in October. 
New/Other Business:  
Green Mountain Book Festival speaker Ethan Tapper (author and forester) on September 19. Civic Reads series 
brings JJ Green, author of The Noise War: How to Find the Truth When Everything Is Lying to Yo u, on Thursday, 
September 24. 
Next meeting: November 18 at 7:45 a.m. 
Adjournment: Becca Thompson moved, Cate MacLachlan seconded. Approved.
